data.name: Space Crash Simulator
data.detailed_description:
Collide planets built from a million interacting particles.

Space Crash Simulator is a real-time planetary collision sandbox built on GPU-accelerated Smoothed Particle Hydrodynamics — the same class of method used in scientific impact simulation. Every planet, star, and fragment is made of individual particles that attract, compress, melt, and break apart under the forces you set up. Nothing is scripted: fragmentation, shock fronts, tidal stretching, moon formation and accretion all emerge from the equations.

There are no missions and no objectives. You set the initial conditions, press play, and watch what physics does with them.

Scale

  • Real-time simulation of hundreds of thousands of particles

  • COMPUTE mode pre-calculates collisions of up to 1,000,000 particles per planet on a modern GPU, streaming to disk for long recordings

  • Replay with rewind, scrubbing, slow motion and reverse — watch the same impact from any angle, as many times as you want

  • Gravity solved with a Barnes-Hut octree: every particle pulls on every other one, at scales where summing the pairs directly would be a trillion interactions per step

Build the bodies

  • Draw your own shapes: sketch a silhouette and extrude or revolve it into a 3D body, with a live preview — then crush it under its own gravity

  • Spheres, hollow spheres, cubes, walls, discs, rings, sieves, and a lattice space-frame that buckles and shears instead of shattering

  • Make any body indestructible: unbreakable walls, unstoppable projectiles

  • Planet textures built in or imported from your own images; procedurally granulated star surfaces

  • Black holes with accretion discs, gravitational lensing, and tidal disruption

Control the physics

  • Particle count, mass, viscosity, rest density

  • Impact velocity, spin, inclination

  • Impact heating, thermal conduction, radiative cooling

  • Orbit presets: circular, elliptical, and Roche-limit — one click puts a moon exactly where you want it

Simulation modes

  • Planetary mode: build a system of planets, moons, walls, black holes and painted shapes, and collide them however you like: head-on impacts, glancing blows, or chaotic multi-body dynamics where tiny differences in setup produce wildly different outcomes

  • Protoplanetary disc + star: accretion and early system evolution

  • Galaxy mode: large-scale gravitational interactions between galactic cores (gravity only; SPH does not apply at that scale)

What this is, and isn't

Space Crash Simulator is an open-ended physics tool for people interested in astrophysics, orbital mechanics, impact dynamics, and scientific visualization, or anyone who wants to build a scenario and watch it play out. There is no storyline, no progression system, and no competitive mechanics. The focus is entirely on constructing situations, adjusting parameters, and observing the physical behaviour that follows.

data.reviews:
“A technically excellent planetary collision simulator… visually spectacular and scientifically fascinating.”
OneDigital

“A rare balance of scientific rigor, entertainment value, and technical optimization.”
Gamer Daily

GameReviews Italy

pc_requirements.minimum:
Minimum:
  • OS: Windows 10
  • Processor: Intel/AMD 2+ Cores (1.7GHz and above)
  • Memory: 8 GB RAM
  • Graphics: Intel HD 4600 (AMD or NVIDIA equivalent)
  • Storage: 10 GB available space

mac_requirements.minimum:
Minimum:
  • OS: macOS 10.15 (or newer)
  • Processor: Intel/Apple Silicon 2+ Cores (1.7GHz and above)
  • Memory: 8 GB RAM
  • Graphics: OpenGL 2.0 or Metal
  • Storage: 10 GB available space
